answer: The authors use Aira-Dojo as the test harness to study agent design choices in the SSL setting, providing a consistent environment for this evaluation [agentssl-2611.17323v1:p3:para350:4].
The agent uses a fixed set of program transformation operators that includes Draft, Debug, Improve, and Analyze operators [agentssl-2611.17323v1:p4:para350:14].

The label budget (number of iterations) for each active selection algorithm on ProgramSelectBench is determined by the formula: min(25, # of classes × # of training images per class) [agentssl-2611.17323v1:p19:para350:8].
The model used in the LLM-as-judge pipeline that analyzes agent-generated programs is GPT-5.4 [agentssl-2611.17323v1:p20:para350:16].
In the DTD 3-shot example, the agent receives a total of 141 labeled training images (3 images per class across 47 categories) and 1739 unlabeled datapoints [agentssl-2611.17323v1:p28:para350:14].

AgentSSL demonstrates strong performance in text classification tasks, exceeding the strongest human-engineered baselines in 8 out of 12 settings by up to +21.8% under weak feedback conditions and matched compute resources [agentssl-2611.17323v1:p1:para350:3]. However, it faces challenges with program selection, where performance can drop by as much as 47% when based on the agent’s feedback metric [agentssl-2611.17323v1:p1:para350:4]. The effectiveness of program selection is critical, as misalignment between the feedback metric and test performance can lead to substantial degradation in results [agentssl-2611.17323v1:p7:para350:3].
